label: rare, context-specific: <DEL> step / after q / early copy step (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.05% of steps). Its activation mass falls into three loose groups: the <DEL> step (32%, enriched for long sequences L>=8 and first token r/o), original-phase steps right after a q input (about 32%, mostly t=2-4), and the copy step with recall_idx=2, where the input is orig(1) (19%, enriched when orig(1) is i/r/o). Even the narrowest clause tested reaches only about 6% precision (<DEL> & first_tok=r & L>=7), so the true trigger is some specific combination of the sequence so far that these token variables do not capture. It never fires at t=0-1 or at recall_idx>=4. Magnitude is about the same across the groups; the largest values are at <DEL> steps in sequences starting with r. The recorded 3-clause disjunction gets about 70% of the mass but under 1% precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=2 & prev_tok=q (+6.06), t=3 & prev_tok=q (+5.87), orig0=r (+3.79), prev_tok=q (+2.69), orig0=2 (+2.61), orig2=u (+2.61). Lower it: prev_tok=r (-4.18), prev3_tok=- (-3.48), phase=2 (-3.16), prev_tok=2 (-2.79).
